subject: physics
title: Kinetic theory of gases
key_idea: Pressure comes from molecules changing momentum at the walls, giving pV = ⅓Nm⟨c²⟩. Comparing this with pV = NkT shows that the mean kinetic energy of a molecule is (3/2)kT, which depends only on temperature.

blocks.text: Kinetic theory explains the behaviour of a gas by the motion of its molecules. This section covers the assumptions and how they give pressure.

items: A gas contains a very large number of molecules in rapid, random motion.
The molecules occupy a negligible volume compared with the volume of the gas.
All collisions, with each other and with the walls, are perfectly elastic.
The time of a collision is negligible compared with the time between collisions.
There are no forces between molecules except during collisions.
A molecule hitting a wall bounces back, so its **momentum changes**.
By Newton's second law, the force on the molecule equals its rate of change of momentum. By Newton's third law, the wall feels an equal and opposite force.
Very many collisions each second give a steady force on the wall.
Pressure is this force divided by the area of the wall.

blocks.text: Brownian motion is evidence for this model. Visible specks in smoke or pollen grains in water move randomly because unseen molecules hit them unevenly.

items: Molecules are point-like, elastic and do not attract each other between collisions.
Pressure comes from the change in momentum of molecules hitting the wall.

blocks.text: Applying Newton's laws to the molecules in a box gives a link between pressure, volume and the speed of the molecules.

items.text: A molecule of mass m moves at speed cₓ along a box of length L. Each wall collision changes its momentum by 2mcₓ.
It hits the same wall every 2L / cₓ, so it hits cₓ / 2L times each second.
Force = change in momentum per second = 2mcₓ × cₓ / 2L = mcₓ² / L.
F = Nm⟨cₓ²⟩ / L, where ⟨cₓ²⟩ is the mean of cₓ² for all the molecules.
p = F / L² = Nm⟨cₓ²⟩ / L³ = Nm⟨cₓ²⟩ / V.
Molecules move randomly in all directions, so ⟨c²⟩ = ⟨cₓ²⟩ + ⟨cᵧ²⟩ + ⟨c_z²⟩ = 3⟨cₓ²⟩, and ⟨cₓ²⟩ = ⅓⟨c²⟩.

blocks.label: Pressure of an ideal gas
where: N is the number of molecules
m is the mass of one molecule (kg)

items.meaning: The mean of the squares of the speeds of the molecules.
The square root of the mean-square speed: c_rms = √⟨c²⟩.

items: pV = ⅓Nm⟨c²⟩ follows from momentum change in one dimension, extended to three.
The rms speed is the square root of the mean-square speed.

blocks.text: Comparing the kinetic theory equation with the equation of state links molecular energy directly to temperature.

blocks.label: Mean translational kinetic energy of a molecule
where: ½m⟨c²⟩ is the mean kinetic energy of one molecule (J)
k is the Boltzmann constant, 1.38 × 10⁻²³ J K⁻¹

items: The mean kinetic energy of a molecule is proportional to the thermodynamic temperature.
Using k = R / N_A, the same result is ½m⟨c²⟩ = 3RT / (2N_A).
In an ideal gas there are no forces between molecules, so there is no potential energy.
The **internal energy** of an ideal gas is therefore the total kinetic energy of its molecules. For a monatomic gas this is (3/2)NkT or (3/2)nRT.
At the same temperature, molecules of lower mass have a higher rms speed.

diagram.alt: A slider that changes temperature and gas to show the mean kinetic energy of a molecule and the root-mean-square speed.

items: ½m⟨c²⟩ = (3/2)kT: mean kinetic energy depends only on temperature.
The internal energy of an ideal gas is the kinetic energy of its molecules.

checks.q: State three assumptions of the kinetic theory of gases.
checks.a: Any three: very many molecules in rapid random motion; molecules have negligible volume compared with the gas; collisions are perfectly elastic; collision time is negligible compared with the time between collisions; no forces between molecules except in collisions.

checks.q: Explain how the molecules of a gas exert a pressure on the walls of a container.
checks.a: Molecules collide with the wall and rebound, so their momentum changes. The force on the wall equals the rate of change of momentum. Many collisions give a steady force; pressure is force divided by area.

checks.q: The mean kinetic energy of a nitrogen molecule at 300 K is 6.2 × 10⁻²¹ J. The mass of a molecule is 4.65 × 10⁻²⁶ kg. Calculate the root-mean-square speed.

items: The gas laws are empirical: they come from experiments. Kinetic theory is a model that arises from theory and explains them.
Brownian motion gave evidence for the existence of atoms and molecules.
Knowledge of gases developed over time: experiments on pressure, volume and temperature came first, and the molecular model explained them later.
The derivation of pV = ⅓Nm⟨c²⟩ is not required, but the equation and its meaning are.
The derivation of ½m⟨c²⟩ = (3/2)kT from pV = ⅓Nm⟨c²⟩ and pV = NkT is required.
The molecules in a gas have a range of speeds, shown by a Maxwell–Boltzmann distribution.
The distribution is not symmetrical. It has a peak and a long tail to high speeds.
No molecules have zero speed, and the area under the curve is the total number of molecules.
At a higher temperature the peak moves to a higher speed, and the curve is lower and wider.
